blocks.x: While some Christmas markets gather together a few vendors, string up a few lights, and call it a day, Christkindlmarkt operates on a completely different scale.

Each holiday season, 10 acres of Bethlehem, Pennsylvania are transformed into a sprawling European winter village. The scent of cinnamon and mulled wine fills the air and thousands of twinkling lights reflect off icy streets as artisans sell handmade treasures.

Over its 30+ year history, the market has expanded to feature over 200 premier artisans and crafters from across the United States, and is one of the select U.S. markets to host the iconic German ornament manufacturer Käthe Wohlfahrt!
Now, the European-style market is returning for its 34th season this fall, running on weekends from November 13 to December 20, 2026 at the SteelStacks Campus.

And sure, we haven’t even reached Halloween yet, so you may be thinking it’s too early to have Christmas on your radar. But this is the kind of massive regional draw you need to lock down on your calendar before the cold weather sets in.

Source / Christkindlmarkt Bethlehem, PA
Three decades of serious national acclaim
Christkindlmarkt began in 1993, heavily inspired by the original open-air German markets designed to celebrate the season with food, warm drinks, and craftsmanship.
Over 34 years, that vision has absolutely exploded in scale.

Today, it occupies the equivalent of three city blocks and curates more than 200 of the nation’s top artisans, making it a destination specifically for those trying to track down gifts for “hard-to-buy-for” friends and family.

That massive footprint, paired with an unmistakable European authenticity, is exactly why it keeps landing in the top tier of USA Today’s “Best Holiday Markets” nationwide and has been highlighted by both Oprah Daily and Travel + Leisure as one of the best holiday markets in the world.
In other words, it’s way more than just a beloved Pennsylvania staple.

Source / ArtsQuest
What you’ll experience after walking in
Bethlehem adds a cinematic edge you won’t find at a typical Alpine pop-up.

The entire market is against the dramatic, 100-year-old ruins of the historic Bethlehem Steel blast furnaces. At night, these towering industrial structures are heavily illuminated, creating a striking backdrop behind the traditional wooden vendor huts, heated tents, and outdoor Winter Wonderland spaces.
It’s easily one of the most picture perfect holiday settings in the country, making it a perfect day trip escape from the city.
Based on past years and 2026 announcements, expect the market’s sprawling lineup to feature:
A dedicated U.S. storefront for the iconic German manufacturer Käthe Wohlfahrt, selling Bavarian-style nutcrackers and storybook ornaments
An interactive Glass Haus where visitors can actually try hot glass ornament-making
Traditional holiday fare ranging from German bratwurst and strudel to European-style poutine and mashed potato balls
Private, rentable igloos for up to six guests, complete with Amish fireplaces and a gallon of hot chocolate
Live entertainment on a permanent outdoor stage, featuring brass groups, strolling carolers, and community choirs
Interactive ice sculpting demonstrations and local spirits tastings
ArtsQuest also hosts special ticketed events throughout the market’s run, like the “Old Fashioned” Christmas experience on select Sundays and a Sip ‘n Shop evening on December 19.

Source / ArtsQuest
A historic slice of Pennsylvania that’s worth an entire day
The market takes over the SteelStacks campus in Bethlehem, roughly 90 minutes west of Manhattan in the Lehigh Valley.
It’s a town that fully leans into its official “Christmas City USA” moniker, making this 10-acre pop-up feel like discovering the capital of the holidays hiding just across the state border.
The surrounding National Historic Landmark District is packed with centuries-old architecture, cobblestone-style charm, and horse-drawn carriage rides that justify building a full itinerary.

And the SteelStacks venue itself is a remarkable setting—when those towering industrial ruins are illuminated at night, it creates one of the most striking and highly-photographed winter backdrops on the East Coast.

Source / ArtsQuest
Tips for visiting the market
Because this is an event that draws visitors from across several states, you have to strategize your visit rather than just winging it.
Target Friday evenings for a deal: If you want to save cash, admission is completely free from 5 pm to 8 pm on Fridays
Ship it from the source: Take advantage of the on-site USPS “Big Blue Box” to flat-rate ship your artisan purchases right from the market instead of hauling them back to the city
Use the free transit: Catch a ride on the free Christmas City Trolley to easily bounce between the SteelStacks grounds and the historic downtown area
Dress in real layers: The venue mixes heated indoor tents with exposed outdoor Winter Wonderland spaces, so prepare for fluctuating temperatures
Book ahead: Pre-book admission and private igloos online well before your trip, as prime weekend slots regularly sell out

Source / Christkindlmarkt Bethlehem, PA
The details
Location: ArtsQuest Center at SteelStacks, PNC Plaza, 101 Founders Way (or 711 E. 1st Street), Bethlehem, PA 18015
Dates: Weekends from November 13 to December 20, 2026 (Open Friday–Sunday in November; Thursday–Sunday in December)
Hours: Thursdays & Sundays: 10 am – 6 pm | Fridays & Saturdays: 10 am – 8 pm
Tickets: Available through the market’s official website (Pro-tip: Admission is typically free on Fridays from 5 pm to 8 pm)
